section_summary: This section documents the State Department’s December 1939 effort to establish a voluntary “moral embargo” against transferring high-octane aviation-gasoline technology to Japan and, ultimately, the Soviet Union. Oil and engineering companies supplied technical assessments, described pending Japanese negotiations, attended a December 14 conference, and generally agreed to withhold processes, patents, plants, and engineering assistance if competitors did likewise. The Department also began monitoring exports of tetraethyl lead and other blending agents, while preparing to answer a possible Japanese protest that the policy violated the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation.

subfiles.title: Continuation of Howard’s assessment of Japanese aviation-gasoline technology
subfiles.from: Frank A. Howard
subfiles.about: Assesses which synthetic-fuel and blending-agent technologies Japan possesses or lacks.
subfiles.summary: Howard states that Japan has not mastered hydrogenation, catalytic cracking, hydroforming, or tetraethyl-lead manufacture. He reports that Japan recently acquired Universal Oil Products technology for iso-octane and selective polymer production, including the necessary simple hydrogenation.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Howard’s November 27 letter
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Howard’s information concerning sales of aviation-gasoline manufacturing rights.
subfiles.summary: Green thanks Howard for his November 27 letter and enclosure regarding the sale of technical information and manufacturing rights. He regrets that their November 20 discussion produced no definite result and says the Department is still considering the matter.

subfiles.title: Telephone call from Frank A. Howard concerning Phillips Petroleum negotiations
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Records Howard’s warning that Phillips Petroleum might shortly license aviation-gasoline technology to Japanese interests.
subfiles.summary: Howard told Green that effective restraint required unanimous agreement among the American companies concerned. He reported Japanese negotiations with Phillips Petroleum and urged the Secretary or Under Secretary to tell company executives collectively that such transfers were contrary to United States interests and policy.

subfiles.title: Shell Oil offer of cooperation and introductions
subfiles.from: R. R. Griffin
subfiles.about: Offers Shell’s cooperation and proposes meetings with senior Shell Union and Universal Oil Products officials.
subfiles.summary: Griffin assures Green that Shell is prepared to assist the Department. He proposes introducing R. van der Woude and arranging contact with H. J. Halle, who was recovering from illness.

subfiles.title: Consultations with Phillips Petroleum and Frank A. Howard
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Identifies the companies whose cooperation was considered necessary to prevent aviation-gasoline technology transfers to Japan.
subfiles.summary: After consulting Maxwell Hamilton, Green contacted Phillips Petroleum and Howard about convening responsible company representatives. Howard supplied three lists of petroleum and engineering firms, distinguishing essential participants from controlled companies and minority-interest holders, and explained Shell Union’s British-Netherlands ownership.

subfiles.title: Phillips Petroleum telegram arranging a Washington contact
subfiles.from: K. S. Adams, Phillips Petroleum Company
subfiles.about: Advises that Don Emery will be available in Washington to represent Phillips Petroleum.
subfiles.summary: Adams responds to Green’s telephone call by identifying Vice President and General Counsel Don Emery as the company’s representative. Emery would be at the Mayflower Hotel on December 7 and could remain for additional days if necessary.

subfiles.title: Argument for permitting the proposed Houdry Process transaction
subfiles.from: E. B. Badger & Sons Company, signed by George C. Hargrove
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, attention Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Presents technical, strategic, and financial arguments for allowing a Houdry Process license to Japanese interests.
subfiles.summary: Badger estimates Japanese refining, cracking, iso-octane, and potential aviation-fuel capacity and argues that a Houdry installation would still leave Japan dependent on suitable crude, blending agents, tetraethyl lead, and American-made catalyst. The company emphasizes American purchases and employment arising from the roughly $5.75 million transaction and recommends completing the negotiations.

subfiles.title: Addenda on Japanese negotiations, hydrogenation, refineries, and iso-octane capacity
subfiles.from: E. B. Badger & Sons Company
subfiles.about: Details current technology negotiations and tabulates Japanese and Manchurian refining capacity.
subfiles.summary: The addendum describes negotiations involving Toa Nenryo, Universal Oil Products, I. G. Farben, and M. W. Kellogg, including planned transfers of patents, designs, and payments. Its tables list refinery equipment and feedstocks in Japan, Korea, and Manchuria and estimate potential Japanese iso-octane output at 428 barrels per day.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs comments on the proposed Houdry sale
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Joseph W. Ballantine
subfiles.about: Challenges Badger’s arguments and recommends a collective meeting with the affected companies.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs questions why Japan would spend more than $5 million if the Houdry installation offered little benefit and disputes Badger’s economic reasoning. It warns that permitting one contract would undermine cooperation by Phillips and other competitors and recommends that the Under Secretary receive all essential firms together.

subfiles.title: George C. Hargrove’s December 7 visit
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Records Hargrove’s appeal for rapid approval of Badger’s proposed Japanese transaction.
subfiles.summary: Hargrove delivered Badger’s December 6 submission and strongly urged the Department not to object to the proposed Houdry transaction. He attributed competitors’ opposition to commercial advantage rather than patriotism and maintained that the sale would not appreciably assist Japanese high-octane gasoline production.

subfiles.title: Conference with Don Emery of Phillips Petroleum
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Records Phillips Petroleum’s conditional willingness to refrain from transferring aviation-gasoline technology to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Green explained the Government’s desire to keep Japan dependent on American purchases of high-test aviation gasoline. Emery said Phillips would cooperate if competitors did likewise, but warned that a Japanese mission would arrive within two weeks to negotiate a contract and therefore prompt action was essential.

subfiles.title: Howard’s warning of imminent Japanese technology purchases
subfiles.from: Charles W. Yost
subfiles.about: Reports Howard’s warning that several Japanese delegations were close to purchasing American aviation-gasoline processes.
subfiles.summary: Howard told Yost that Japanese delegations were negotiating with several American firms. He believed the Department had only three or four days to prevent the sales before Japan acquired the essential information, and Yost replied that a decision was imminent.

subfiles.title: Calls from Hargrove and Griffin urging immediate action
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Records warnings from Badger and Shell representatives that immediate action was required.
subfiles.summary: Hargrove telephoned from Philadelphia and Griffin from New York. Both said the Department would have to act immediately if it wished to prevent sales of high-test aviation-gasoline manufacturing rights to Japanese interests.

subfiles.title: Griffin radiogram concerning the December 14 meeting
subfiles.from: R. R. Griffin
subfiles.about: Confirms Griffin’s attendance or availability for the meeting in Room 360 the following day.
subfiles.summary: Griffin sends a terse radiogram referring to the next day’s meeting in Room 360. The message forms part of the companies’ responses to the Department’s December 12 summons.

subfiles.title: Sun Oil confirmation of attendance
subfiles.from: Arthur E. Pew Jr., Sun Oil Company
subfiles.about: Confirms that a Sun Oil representative will attend the requested December meeting.
subfiles.summary: Pew states that Sun Oil’s representative will attend the meeting in Room 360 of the State Building. He refers expressly to the Department’s telegram of December 12.

subfiles.title: M. W. Kellogg confirmation of attendance
subfiles.from: M. W. Kellogg Company
subfiles.about: Names Vice President F. E. Johnson Jr. as the company’s representative at the December 14 meeting.
subfiles.summary: The company advises Welles that F. E. Johnson Jr. will attend Thursday’s meeting at 11:30 a.m. Johnson was M. W. Kellogg’s vice president.

subfiles.title: E. B. Badger & Sons confirmation of attendance
subfiles.from: E. B. Badger & Sons Company
subfiles.about: Confirms that a company representative will meet the Under Secretary on December 14.
subfiles.summary: Badger advises Hull that its representative will attend the 11:30 a.m. meeting in Room 360 of the Department of State building. The message responds to the Department’s December 12 wire.

subfiles.title: Transfer to Moral Embargo file
subfiles.from: Department of State filing office
subfiles.about: Records the transfer or cross-reference of material to the Department’s moral-embargo file.
subfiles.summary: The sheet directs that the referenced item be transferred to decimal file 700.00116, Moral Embargo/9. It contains no substantive discussion of the transaction.

subfiles.title: Shell Union acceptance of the Department’s policy
subfiles.from: R. van der Woude
subfiles.about: Assures the Department that Shell Union and its affiliates will support its wishes.
subfiles.summary: Van der Woude acknowledges Green’s December 19 letter and enclosed memorandum. He says the memorandum is clear and promises full support from Shell Union and its affiliates.

subfiles.title: Report on the December 14 oil-company conference
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Reports the participants, disclosures, debate, and agreements reached at the aviation-gasoline conference.
subfiles.summary: Representatives of nine companies met Berle, Hornbeck, and Green for two and a half hours and disclosed existing or contemplated Japanese contracts. All expressed willingness to cooperate, often conditionally on universal compliance, and agreed on a memorandum restricting technology transfers while the Department considered extending the policy to the Soviet Union and monitoring blending-agent exports.

subfiles.title: Japan-specific aviation-gasoline policy memorandum
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: States the agreed policy against further delivery of high-quality aviation-gasoline technology to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum asks nine firms to withhold plans, plants, patents, processes, manufacturing rights, technical information, and engineering assistance from Japanese interests. It also directs fourteen producers and exporters to report shipments or contemplated shipments of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylates to Japan.

subfiles.title: Generic-country version of the aviation-gasoline policy
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Restates the transfer and reporting policy without naming the countries to which it applied.
subfiles.summary: This version substitutes “certain countries” for Japan and asks the nine companies to withhold aviation-gasoline technology from their representatives or use. It similarly requests current information from fourteen companies about blending-agent shipments to unnamed countries.

subfiles.title: Signed Japan-specific departmental memorandum
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Provides a signed version of the policy withholding aviation-gasoline technology from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Green’s memorandum repeats the request that nine firms stop further transfers of relevant plants, rights, patents, processes, information, and engineering assistance to Japan. It also identifies fourteen companies from which the Department sought current data on Japanese imports of strategic blending agents.

subfiles.title: Signed modified policy for unnamed countries
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Presents the signed, country-neutral version of the technology-transfer policy.
subfiles.summary: The modified text applies the restriction to “certain countries” and permits companies to cite the Department’s request when suspending negotiations or commitments. It retains the proposed monitoring of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylate exports by fourteen named companies.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of policy memorandum to R. van der Woude
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Sends Shell Union the country-neutral memorandum implementing the December 14 decisions.
subfiles.summary: Green encloses the memorandum adopted following the December 14 meeting. He explains that although it names no country, its policy applies separately and jointly to the two countries considered at the meeting.

subfiles.title: Request to Standard Oil Company of New Jersey for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Standard Oil Company of New Jersey
subfiles.about: Requests past and prospective export data for specified blending agents sent to Japan or the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks for 1939 statistics on exports of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylates to Japan and the Soviet Union. It also requests continuing reports of future or contemplated sales to either country.

subfiles.title: Request to the Texas Company for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests information on blending-agent exports to Japan and the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: The Department requests figures for the Texas Company’s 1939 exports of four aviation-fuel blending agents to the two countries. It also asks the company to report future sales or contemplated exports.

subfiles.title: Request to Gulf Refining Company for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Seeks current and future information on strategic blending-agent exports.
subfiles.summary: Green asks Gulf for statistics on 1939 exports of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylates to Japan and the Soviet Union. The company is also asked to report later sales or prospective sales to those destinations.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of policy memorandum to E. B. Badger
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Sends Badger the memorandum implementing decisions from the December 14 conference.
subfiles.summary: Green encloses the agreed memorandum for Badger’s information and action. He notes that the unnamed policy applies to both countries specially considered at the meeting.

subfiles.title: Request to Phillips Petroleum for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests statistics and continuing reports on blending-agent exports to Japan and the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks Phillips for 1939 export quantities of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylates. It also seeks reports on future or contemplated sales to Japan or the Soviet Union.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of policy memorandum to Sun Oil Company
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Sun Oil Company, attention Harry Heller
subfiles.about: Notifies Sun Oil of the decisions arising from the December 14 conference.
subfiles.summary: Green sends Sun Oil the memorandum recording the conference decisions and requests appropriate action. He explains that its unnamed restrictions apply to each and both of the two countries discussed.

subfiles.title: Request to Tidewater Associated Oil for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests past and future export information concerning aviation-fuel blending agents.
subfiles.summary: The Department requests Tidewater’s 1939 statistics for exports of four blending agents to Japan and the Soviet Union. It additionally asks for continuing information about future or contemplated sales.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of policy memorandum to Frank A. Howard
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Sends Standard Oil Development Company the memorandum based on the December 14 decisions.
subfiles.summary: Green encloses the policy memorandum for Howard’s information and action. He clarifies that, although no nation is named, the policy applies to both countries considered by the Department and company representatives.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of policy memorandum to F. E. Johnson
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: F. E. Johnson, M. W. Kellogg Company
subfiles.about: Sends M. W. Kellogg the country-neutral memorandum implementing the conference’s decisions.
subfiles.summary: Green forwards the memorandum for Johnson’s information and appropriate action. He states that the unnamed policy applies to each and both of the two countries discussed on December 14.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of policy memorandum to Phillips Petroleum
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Notifies Phillips Petroleum of the aviation-gasoline technology policy adopted after the December 14 meeting.
subfiles.summary: Green encloses the memorandum setting out the conference decisions and requests compliance. He advises that its country-neutral language covers both countries specially considered.

subfiles.title: Request to Pan American Refining for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests export statistics and continuing reports for four strategic blending agents.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks Pan American Refining for its 1939 sales for export to Japan and the Soviet Union. It also requests later information on prospective sales of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylates.

subfiles.title: Request to Standard Oil Company of California for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Seeks information on blending-agent shipments to Japan and the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks Standard Oil of California to report its 1939 export quantities of four aviation-fuel blending agents. It requests further reports when the company makes or contemplates similar sales to either country.

subfiles.title: Request to Socony-Vacuum for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests statistics and prospective information on strategic blending-agent exports.
subfiles.summary: Green seeks data on Socony-Vacuum’s 1939 exports of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylates to Japan and the Soviet Union. He also asks for reports on future or contemplated transactions.

subfiles.title: Request to Shell Union Oil for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests past and future information concerning blending-agent exports to Japan and the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks Shell Union for statistical information covering its 1939 exports of four blending agents. It also seeks notice of later sales or prospective sales to either of the named countries.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of policy memorandum to Socony-Vacuum
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Socony-Vacuum Oil Company, attention Dallas Lamont
subfiles.about: Sends Socony-Vacuum the memorandum arising from the December 14 meeting.
subfiles.summary: Green encloses the conference memorandum for the company’s information and action. He explains that the policy, although country-neutral on its face, applies to both countries under consideration.

subfiles.title: Request to Atlantic Refining for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests export information for specified aviation-fuel blending agents.
subfiles.summary: The Department seeks Atlantic’s 1939 export figures for sales to Japan and the Soviet Union. It also asks the company to report future or contemplated sales of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylates.

subfiles.title: Request to Ethyl Gasoline Corporation for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests information on 1939 and prospective exports of strategic blending agents.
subfiles.summary: Green asks Ethyl Gasoline Corporation for export quantities sent to Japan and the Soviet Union during 1939. The letter also requests continuing information concerning future or contemplated sales.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of policy memorandum to H. J. Halle
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Sends Universal Oil Products’ president the memorandum implementing the December 14 decisions.
subfiles.summary: Green encloses the agreed memorandum for Halle’s information and action. He says that the policy’s unnamed restrictions apply to each and both of the two countries considered.

subfiles.title: Request to Standard Oil Company of Indiana for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests current and continuing information on blending-agent exports to Japan and the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks the company to disclose its 1939 exports of four aviation-fuel blending agents to the two countries. It also requests information on future or contemplated export sales.

subfiles.title: Request to Cities Service Export Company for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Seeks statistics and continuing reports about strategic blending-agent exports.
subfiles.summary: Green requests figures for the company’s 1939 exports of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylates to Japan and the Soviet Union. He asks that later sales or contemplated transactions also be reported.

subfiles.title: Request to Sinclair Refining Company for blending-agent export data
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests information on past and prospective exports of aviation-fuel blending agents.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks Sinclair for statistics on its 1939 exports to Japan and the Soviet Union. It also requests ongoing information about later sales or contemplated exports of the four listed agents.

subfiles.title: Ethyl Gasoline Corporation report on tetraethyl-lead exports
subfiles.from: Ralph C. Champlin, Ethyl Gasoline Corporation
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, attention Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Reports known tetraethyl-lead shipments to Japan and the absence of shipments to the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: Champlin reports no known 1939 shipments to the Soviet Union, but states that 462,000 pounds of Ethyl fluid containing 283,716 pounds of tetraethyl lead went to Japan through April 30. Later shipments were handled by the British Associated Ethyl Company, and Ethyl also knew of three shipments totaling 147,000 gallons of leaded gasoline.

subfiles.title: Request for monthly Ethyl reports and details of leaded-gasoline exports
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests follow-up information and monthly reporting on tetraethyl-lead shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Green asks Champlin to forward Associated Ethyl’s figures for shipments since April 30 and to report future Japanese sales monthly. He also requests the names of exporters and any other available details concerning the three known shipments of gasoline blended with Ethyl fluid.

subfiles.title: Standard Oil of New Jersey report of no relevant exports
subfiles.from: Standard Oil Company of New Jersey, signed by L. K. Beood
subfiles.about: Reports no 1939 sales of alkylates or blending agents to Japan or the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: Standard Oil states that neither it nor its affiliates sold the relevant products to Japan or the Soviet Union during 1939. It referred the Department’s inquiry to Standard-Vacuum Oil Company for information on any shipments that concern might have made.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Standard Oil of New Jersey’s export report
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Standard Oil Company of New Jersey
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the company’s report that it made no relevant exports during 1939.
subfiles.summary: Green records Standard Oil’s statement that it sold no alkylates or blending agents to Japan or the Soviet Union in 1939. He also notes that Standard-Vacuum would communicate separately about its own shipments.

subfiles.title: M. W. Kellogg acceptance of the December 14 decisions
subfiles.from: F. E. Johnson Jr., M. W. Kellogg Company
subfiles.about: Promises that M. W. Kellogg will follow the Department’s agreed aviation-gasoline policy.
subfiles.summary: Johnson acknowledges Green’s December 19 letter and the memorandum recording the December 14 decisions. He promises full cooperation and says the company will consult the Department if questions or ambiguities arise.

subfiles.title: Proposed reply to a Japanese protest against the moral embargo
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Joseph W. Ballantine
subfiles.about: Proposes arguments rebutting a possible Japanese claim that the moral embargo violated the 1911 commercial treaty.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum recommends telling the Japanese Ambassador that manufacturers’ compliance is voluntary, the public statements name no country, and the policy condemns attacks on civilian populations while conserving strategic technical information. It argues that soliciting voluntary cooperation from American exporters does not infringe the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation, while noting that any written protest would require a response tailored to its contents.
